title: egress policy orchestrator and DNS consistency probe for control plane VPCs
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add Egress Policy Orchestrator module that centralizes controlplane egress rules, route attachments, and a DNS consistency probe. Includes Terraform module, Helm values, and upgrade/rollback hooks.
description: Summary: Adds a new Egress Policy Orchestrator (EPO) and a DNS consistency probe to the private installer. The EPO centralizes how control plane VPCs advertise and enforce outbound egress policies (SGs, NAT/egress gateway attachments, route table tagging) and provides a lightweight reconciliation loop that prevents accidental open egress. The DNS probe validates conditional forwarding/mirror zones used by the control plane endpoints and triggers a controlled retry/rollback when DNS stitching fails. Motivation: Recent upgrades surfaced a class of failures where staggered endpoint updates left control plane instances with mismatched DNS resolution and transient open egress paths. This PR provides guardrails so upgrades and capacity operations have deterministic egress and DNS behavior. What changed: - New Terraform module terraform/modules/egress-orchestrator: orchestration state, role bindings, security-group templates, route overrides, and optional NAT attachment stub. - Installer chart changes helm/redwood-private-installer: values for egress profiles, healthProbe sidecar config for DNS probe, and rollout hooks for staged egress cutover. - Upgrade/rollback tooling: preflight plan, plan-check runner, and a safe-rollback script that reverses route and SG changes and re-applies previous DNS mirror entries. - Integration test harness updates in benchmark-lab to simulate cross-account Route53 forwarding flaps. Backwards compatibility: The EPO is opt-in via values.egressOrchestrator.enabled=false by default to avoid changing existing installs. When enabled, the module attempts to adopt resources annotated with installer:managed=true; resources without annotation are left untouched. Rollout plan: 1) Enable in non-prod and run e2e with controlplane az-failure injection. 2) Monitor DNS probe metrics (probe.success_rate, probe.latency_ms) and egress-change events for 48h. 3) Gradual enablement to prod as a staged release: 10% -> 50% -> 100% node pools. Safety and rollback: - All route and SG changes are applied with a staggered drain window and pre/post hooks. - If the DNS probe fails >5% of checks for 15min, the orchestrator marks the change as contested and automatically reverts to the prior route/SG state while alerting on-call. - A manual rollback script is provided under installer/scripts/rollback-egress.sh with audit-friendly output. Testing performed: - Local terraform plan/apply in a simulated VPC - Helm chart linting and a dry-run end-to-end install in a staging account - Integration test that simulates conditional Route53 forwarding mismatch and validates the probe triggers rollback - Unit tests for the orchestrator reconciliation loop - CI: terraform fmt/lint, helm lint, unit tests, and a targeted e2e run (all green on final run) Related work: ENG-4219 (egress hardening), ENG-4290 (dns-stitching-flakiness). Checklist: - [x] Terraform module with inputs/outputs and examples - [x] Helm values and rollout hooks - [x] Automated DNS probe + metrics - [x] Safety rollback script + docs - [x] Tests and CI green

review_comments: Marco Li: Overall this looks sensible. A few concerns: ensure the module won't inadvertently adopt unannotated SGs in customer accounts. Can we make the adopter stricter?
Aisha Patel: Good point — updated module accepts an adoption_mode variable (none|annotated|force) and defaulted to annotated. I added tests that assert no adoption occurs when none is set.
Sofia Nguyen: How does the probe affect bootstrap time? We need observed latency numbers and a knob for probe timeout.
Aisha Patel: The probe runs in parallel and defaults to a 3s timeout; added values.egressOrchestrator.dnsProbe.timeoutMs and documented expected boot delays (sub-200ms typical, 99th 1.2s in staging).
Ben Turner: CI flakes in the first run — terraform plan-check timed out on large state. Suggest increasing timeout and improving plan-check logging.
Aisha Patel: Increased plan-check timeout to 20m and added more verbose logs for plan diffs. CI rerun is green. Approving now.
Marco Li: Approved after the adoption_mode and plan-check timeout changes.
